item.title: Coordination-Mediated Decoupling-Reconstruction Enables Semisolid Phase Regeneration of Spent Cathodes
item.description:
پارادایم بازتولید نیمه‌جامد با واسطه کمپلکس اگزالات، کاتد مستعمل LiFePO4 را به LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 با ظرفیت 156.5 mAh g–1 و حفظ 91.2% ظرفیت پس از 1000 چرخه تبدیل می‌کند.
Nano Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a coordination-mediated semisolid regeneration paradigm that directly reconstructs spent LiFePO4 into high-performance LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 via oxalate-coordinated selective decoupling and proton-assisted lattice deconstruction. Significance: this chemistry-guided upcycling avoids elemental recovery, yields a structurally ordered cathode with 156.5 mAh g–1 and 91.2% retention after 1000 cycles, advancing sustainable battery recycling.
🏷 LiFePO4 cathode · battery recycling · semisolid regeneration · oxalate coordination · LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4

item.title: Beyond Cathode‐Limited Chemistry: Electrolyte‐Sourced Multielectron Iodine Redox Coupled With Interfacial Zn Regulation in Cathode‐Free Zn – I 2 Batteries
item.description:

Small Structures | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in using choline chloride electrolyte additive to activate reversible high-valent iodine redox in cathode-free Zn–I₂ batteries, moving beyond the two-electron pathway while simultaneously stabilizing the Zn interface. This dual-function strategy suppresses parasitic reactions and enables 2000 h Zn plating/stripping and 90% capacity retention after 5000 cycles, offering a practical electrolyte-engineering route to high-energy, long-life cathode-free batteries.
🏷 cathode-free Zn-I2 battery · choline chloride electrolyte · iodine redox · Zn interface · multielectron chemistry

item.title: Relationship Between Coprecipitation Conditions, Calcination, and Cycling Performance of NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 Cathodes for Sodium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:

Small Structures | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This study uniquely links the full NFM111 synthesis chain—coprecipitation, calcination, and electrochemistry—rather than studying precursor or cathode separately. Optimal conditions (pH 10.8, 0.5 M NH₃, 50 °C; 900 °C calcination) yielded 149 mAh/g and 75–83% retention over 65 cycles. Favorable morphology and narrow size distribution proved critical, partially compensating for secondary phases, and >4.0 V degradation was tied to outgassing and particle fracture.
🏷 sodium-ion battery · NFM111 cathode · coprecipitation · calcination · cycling stability
